name: Microsoft Corporation
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Microsoft crossed $100B of Azure revenue (FY2026, +41%) with a $678B commercial backlog (+84%) underwriting a ~$190B calendar-2026 capex plan (~$175B after an accounting reclassification) — and its marquee energy bets are nuclear-shaped: the ~835 MW Three Mile Island restart (accelerating toward 2027 with a $1B federal loan) and the world's first fusion PPA (Helion, ≥50 MW targeting 2028). Notably, no major 2025–26 standalone battery-storage procurement has surfaced. BACKGROUND: Founded 1975; fiscal years end June 30. FY2026 revenue $331.8B (+18%), net income $133.7B; Microsoft Cloud >$214B; M365 Copilot passed 30M paid seats. The OpenAI relationship was restructured October 2025: ~27% stake (~$135B), an incremental $250B Azure purchase commitment from OpenAI, right-of-first-refusal dropped, IP rights through 2032.
ecosystemRole: We assess Microsoft as the ecosystem's grid-firmness buyer par excellence — and its most conspicuous BESS gap. The Fairwater Atlanta design deliberately runs on resilient grid power with no on-site generators or UPS (4x9 availability at 3x9 cost), meaning Microsoft buys firmness upstream: TMI/Crane nuclear (835 MW), the record 10.5 GW Brookfield renewables framework, a ~40 GW clean-energy portfolio, and fusion options. Its known storage work is older grid-interactive UPS pilots (Dublin, with Eaton) it said it would replicate worldwide — a stated intent BESS suppliers can still sell into.

productsAndServices.name: Azure & AI Infrastructure (Fairwater)
productsAndServices.description: Azure surpassed $100B revenue in FY2026 (+41%; Q4 +43%, accelerating). Fairwater campuses: Wisconsin (Mount Pleasant — 'world's most powerful AI datacenter,' hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, closed-loop liquid cooling) and Atlanta (live October 2025; ~140 kW racks, 1,360 kW rows, GB200/GB300, grid-only power design) linked by a dedicated AI-WAN (120,000 new fiber miles) into the first 'planet-scale AI superfactory' (~2 GW multi-site cluster per trade press); international Fairwater-class builds with nScale in Norway (Narvik) and the UK (Loughton). Maia 200 in-house inference accelerator launched January 2026 (delayed from 2025; Microsoft explicitly says it 'will not replace Nvidia or AMD').
highlights: Commercial RPO $678B (+84%) — the demand backlog that answers the oversupply debate as far as Microsoft is concerned

Calendar-2026 capex ~$190B announced April 2026 (vs $154.6B consensus — a ~$35B shock, ~$25B of it memory-price inflation); later restated to ~$175B via a 25-year useful-life/lease-treatment change, not a real cut
The TD Cowen lease-cancellation story (up to ~2 GW walked, early 2025) resolved as pacing, not retreat — capex re-accelerated through FY2026
Azure decelerations (39% in Q2 FY2026) drew a −5% selloff; Q4's 43% re-acceleration drove +8% — Azure growth is the single number the stock trades on
productsAndServices.positioning: The #2 cloud by revenue with the deepest enterprise franchise; the OpenAI restructuring trades exclusivity for $250B of committed Azure purchases plus freedom to pursue AGI independently
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cloud consumption, enterprise agreements, Copilot seats (30M+ paid)
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Enterprises, OpenAI (anchor), governments, consumers via Copilot
productsAndServices.roadmap: Additional identical Fairwater sites under construction; FY2027 capex guided higher (sell-side chatter of $255–260B is not company guidance)

productsAndServices.name: Energy Procurement (Nuclear-Weighted)
productsAndServices.description: 20-year PPA for the full ~835 MW output of Three Mile Island Unit 1, restarting as the Crane Clean Energy Center — originally 2028, accelerated toward 2027 with a $1B DOE loan, NRC waiver, and FERC clearance (restart pending as of mid-2026). Helion fusion PPA (≥50 MW, targeting 2028; Helion raised $465M at $15.5B valuation to build the plant, cleared first US fusion regulatory licenses; Scientific American and others remain skeptical of the timeline). Brookfield global framework: 10.5+ GW of new renewables 2026–2030 (the largest corporate clean-power framework). ~40 GW clean-energy portfolio; 100% of FY2025 consumption renewable-matched; 20-year Chevron power deal for a Texas data center (June 2026). Grid posture: MISO grid-modernization partnership; signatory of the White House/EPA Ratepayer Protection Pledge.
highlights: The TMI restart is the sector's marquee nuclear-restart transaction — its 2027 delivery is a watch item for the whole nuclear-for-AI thesis

Storage gap: no major 2025–26 standalone BESS procurement found by either research pass; known work is the 2022 Dublin grid-interactive UPS pilot (with Eaton) that Microsoft called 'proven' and pledged to replicate worldwide, and a Swedish DC where BESS replaced diesel
The Atlanta no-UPS/no-genset design shifts resilience spend from facility equipment to grid procurement — a structural choice with direct BESS-market implications
productsAndServices.positioning: Top-tier corporate clean-energy buyer (~40 GW, closing on Amazon's #1); uniquely fusion-forward; distinctly light on named battery storage relative to Amazon/Google
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Counterparties: Constellation, Brookfield, Helion, Chevron, utilities
productsAndServices.roadmap: Crane restart ~2027; Helion ≥50 MW ~2028; Brookfield deliveries 2026–2030

productsAndServices.name: Productivity, Windows & Gaming
productsAndServices.description: Productivity & Business Processes ($37.8B in Q4 FY2026, +14%), Windows/devices/gaming ($12.9B, −4%), and the Copilot layer across all of it. The cash engine that lets Microsoft outspend on infrastructure without Meta-style FCF collapse.
highlights: M365 Copilot 30M+ paid seats (from 20M a quarter earlier) — the clearest enterprise AI monetization datapoint among the big four

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2026 Q4: revenue $90.0B (+18%) and adj. EPS $4.74 beat; Azure +43% and >$100B FY; RPO $678B (+84%); capex held at plan — stock +8%
recentDevelopments.read: The quarter that re-validated the buildout: backlog growth outpacing capex growth is Microsoft's core answer to the oversupply debate.

recentDevelopments.headline: NRC waiver and FERC clearance advance the Three Mile Island (Crane) restart toward 2027
recentDevelopments.read: Every regulatory gate passed so far on an accelerated timeline — the restart's success or slip calibrates the entire nuclear-restart pipeline hyperscalers are counting on.

recentDevelopments.headline: The $190B capex shock: calendar-2026 plan ~$190B vs $154.6B consensus (~$25B of the gap from memory-price inflation)
recentDevelopments.read: Repriced AI capex expectations market-wide; later restated to ~$175B purely via accounting (25-year useful lives, lease treatment) — the real plan held.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2026 Q2: beat on headline but Azure decelerated to 39% — ~5% selloff on capex-vs-growth anxiety
recentDevelopments.read: The cycle's recurring pattern in miniature: Azure's growth rate, not absolute results, sets the market's tolerance for spending.

recentDevelopments.headline: Maia 200 inference accelerator launched (delayed from 2025); Microsoft: it 'will not replace Nvidia or AMD'
recentDevelopments.read: Custom silicon as cost-relief, not independence — Microsoft remains the most NVIDIA-committed hyperscaler at the frontier.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'AI superfactory': Fairwater Wisconsin + Atlanta linked by a dedicated AI-WAN (120,000 fiber miles) into one distributed training machine (~2 GW per trade press)
recentDevelopments.read: Multi-site distributed training changes siting economics — grid diversity becomes a compute-architecture feature, and the Atlanta no-UPS design shows where resilience spend went.

recentDevelopments.headline: Neocloud capacity wave: $9.7B five-year IREN contract (GB300 at Childress, TX) and a multibillion-dollar Lambda agreement signed the same day
recentDevelopments.read: Microsoft is leasing GPU capacity from the neocloud tier at state-program scale — backstopping Azure supply for the OpenAI era without owning every site.

recentDevelopments.headline: OpenAI restructuring: ~27%/$135B stake; OpenAI commits an incremental $250B of Azure purchases; ROFR dropped; IP through 2032; AGI claims independently verified
recentDevelopments.read: Microsoft traded exclusivity for committed spend and optionality — the cleanest resolution available to the cycle's most-watched dependency.

recentDevelopments.headline: Fairwater Wisconsin unveiled as 'the world's most powerful AI datacenter'; Norway and UK AI-DC partnerships announced
recentDevelopments.read: The flagship of the ~$80B→$190B capex arc — closed-loop cooling with near-zero water use is the sustainability counter-argument in physical form.

recentDevelopments.headline: Nebius agreement: ~$17.4B of dedicated GPU capacity through 2031 (options to ~$19.4B), served from Vineland, NJ
recentDevelopments.read: The template of the neocloud-offtake strategy — dedicated capacity, investment-grade paper the counterparty then borrows against.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Microsoft's demand case is the best-documented of the big four: a $678B commercial backlog growing faster (+84%) than capex means its buildout is substantially pre-sold — the OpenAI $250B Azure commitment alone underwrites years of Fairwater capacity. Basis: FY2026 filings.

(High confidence) We assess Microsoft has structurally chosen grid procurement over on-site storage: the Atlanta Fairwater no-UPS/no-genset design plus nuclear/fusion/renewables frameworks put resilience spend upstream of the fence line. For BESS suppliers this makes Microsoft's utilities and grid partners the sales channel — and the pledged worldwide replication of the Dublin grid-interactive UPS concept the door still ajar.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the TMI/Crane restart is the single most consequential energy milestone in Microsoft's book: on-time 2027 delivery validates the restart playbook (and the $1B federal-loan model); slippage would push firming demand toward gas and storage across the sector.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the capex accounting restatement (~$190B → ~$175B via 25-year useful lives and lease treatment) is optics management, not retrenchment — the physical build plan held, and Amy Hood's steady-guidance posture at Q4 was rewarded with the +8% move.

(Low confidence) Sell-side chatter of $255–260B calendar-2027 capex and the reported Helion–OpenAI fusion negotiations are unconfirmed — the latter would dilute Microsoft's first-customer position in fusion if realized.

relationships.note: ~27% stake (~$135B) plus an incremental $250B Azure commitment under the October 2025 'next chapter' agreement.
relationships.context: The restructured partnership (announced Oct 28-30, 2025) gives Microsoft ~27% of OpenAI Group PBC while OpenAI contracted an incremental $250B of Azure purchases — and removed Microsoft's right of first refusal, opening OpenAI to multi-cloud procurement. An April 2026 overhaul then capped the 20% revenue share (through 2030), made the IP license (through 2032) explicitly non-exclusive, and replaced the AGI trigger with fixed dates. Simultaneously investor, largest supplier, and — as OpenAI buys AWS and Google capacity — a loosening anchor.

relationships.note: Largest capacity supplier relationship in the neocloud tier — Microsoft was 67% of CoreWeave's FY2025 revenue.
relationships.context: Microsoft remained CoreWeave's dominant customer through FY2025 at 67% of revenue (up from 62% in 2024) — the single biggest commercial fact about CoreWeave, and the model for Microsoft's neocloud-offtake strategy: lease dedicated GPU capacity on long contracts rather than build every site.

relationships.note: ~$17.4B five-year GPU capacity agreement through 2031 (options to ~$19.4B) from Vineland, NJ.
relationships.context: Signed September 8, 2025: dedicated capacity served from Nebius's DataOne-developed Vineland, NJ data center, deployed in tranches through 2026. The contract's cash flows collateralize Nebius's first secured debt facility ($775M, July 2026) — Microsoft's investment-grade offtake is what makes the neocloud financeable.

relationships.note: $9.7B five-year AI cloud contract — GB300 capacity across four 50MW liquid-cooled 'Horizon' data centers at Childress, TX.
relationships.context: Announced November 3, 2025 with a 20% prepayment and phased delivery through 2026: Horizon 1 was delivered and accepted in August 2026, Horizon 2 is commissioning, Horizons 3-4 target Q4 2026. Goldman Sachs/JPMorgan financed ~96% of the associated GPU capex against the contract — the same offtake-to-financing template as Nebius.

relationships.note: Multibillion-dollar multi-year AI infrastructure agreement — tens of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs including GB300 NVL72.
relationships.context: Announced November 3, 2025 (the same day as the IREN deal), extending an 8+ year relationship dating to 2018. Lambda's subsequent raises — the $1.5B+ Series E and 2026 debt facilities — are explicitly tied to funding deployments for this contract, including ~$1B of JPMorgan-arranged debt for chips Lambda leases to Microsoft.

relationships.note: Tri-party Anthropic partnership: up to 1 GW of Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin on Azure, NVIDIA investing up to $10B.
relationships.context: November 2025: Microsoft, NVIDIA and Anthropic announced a partnership committing Anthropic initially to up to 1 GW of NVIDIA capacity on Azure with NVIDIA investing up to $10B — gigawatt-denominated demand landing on Microsoft's cloud, alongside NVIDIA's role as Microsoft's dominant accelerator supplier.
